question: A can complete a task in 30 days, and B can complete the same task in 40 days. They work together for 10 days, and then C joins them and completes the remaining work in 5 days. How long will C alone take to complete the task?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(30, 40) = 120 units.

Efficiency of A = 4, B = 3 ⇒ Combined efficiency of A + B = 7 units/day.

Work done by A and B in 10 days = 10 × 7 = 70 units.

Remaining 50 units done by A, B, and C in 5 days ⇒ A + B + C efficiency = 50 ÷ 5 = 10 units/day.

C's efficiency = 10 − 7 = 3 units/day ⇒ C alone takes = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the task = 30 days

Time taken by B to complete the task = 40 days

A and B work together for 10 days, and then C joins them to complete the remaining work in 5 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 30

 4
 
 

 B
 40
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of A + B = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day

⇒ Work completed by A and B in 10 days = 10 × 7 = 70 units

⇒ Remaining work = 120 − 70 = 50 units

⇒ C joins A and B, and they complete the remaining 50 units in 5 days together.

⇒ Efficiency of A + B + C = Remaining Work ÷ Days taken = 50 ÷ 5 = 10 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) − Efficiency of (A + B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 10 − 7 = 3 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone to complete the total work = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 days

**∴ The correct answer is 40 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done by individuals. If everyone works for the exact same number of days, the wages can be directly distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept is identical to Time & Work. The only difference is that an inlet pipe has a positive efficiency (filling the tank), while an outlet pipe or leak has a negative efficiency (emptying the tank).

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, first calculate the total work done in a complete cycle (e.g., A works on day 1, B on day 2 → 1 cycle = 2 days). Use this to find out how many complete cycles are required to finish the work.
